SECTION 1

* Young people are often criticized by older generations for spending money on things like holidays and meals out, when they should be saving everything for a house.

* It's becoming nearly impossible for young people to buy homes in the UK because property prices are too high, there aren't enough houses available, and banks won't lend as much money as they used to.

* Young people end up paying all their money to landlords for rent instead of building their own wealth through home ownership, while being blamed for being irresponsible with money.

* Under-25s in the UK earn significantly less than older workers—getting paid as little as £5.60-£7.05 per hour instead of the higher minimum wage given to adults, even when doing exactly the same job.

* Young workers are more likely to have unstable zero-hours contracts and might earn only around £14,500 per year full-time, making it even harder for them to save money for anything, including a home.
